news.title: Six host nations seal places at Fifa World Cup 2030
news.lede: Six nations have already secured qualification for the 2030 Fifa World Cup after being confirmed as hosts of the tournament, despite it being four years away. Morocco, Spain and Portugal, which will jointly host the majority of the expanded 48-team tournament, have qualified automatically. Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay have also secured their places after Fifa awarded each nation one of the tournament's three centenary opening matches, marking the 100th anniversary of the inaugural Fifa World Cup, held in Uruguay in 1930. The 2030 World Cup will be the first to be staged across three continents.

news.title: Cristian Volpato: Australia midfielder allegedly tests positive for cocaine after speeding in Sydney
news.lede: Volpato switched allegiances from Italy to Australia in May. Socceroos World Cup star Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after police twice stopped him for speeding in Sydney on the same night. The 22-year-old Australia midfielder was stopped in a BMW Coupe on the Anzac Bridge at 11:05pm local time on Thursday night after he was caught travelling between 86-94km/h in a 60km/h zone, police said. He was subjected to a roadside breath test, which returned a negative result.

news.title: Kalshi cashes in with US$27 billion World Cup windfall, but legal issues remain
news.lede: Prediction market start-up Kalshi scored well during the ⁠2026 Fifa World Cup, ⁠netting roughly double its projected user ⁠traffic and trading volume as fans scrambled to turn their football savvy into profits. Kalshi recorded US$27 billion in trading volume and saw about three million users during the length of the tournament, a source familiar with the matter said. The competition ran its expanded 48-team format this year and became the most lucrative in Fifa’s history. The source said the start-up had expected US$13 billion in volume and about 1.5 million users during the tournament, which opened at Azteca Stadium in Mexico and ended in New Jersey, where Spain beat Lionel Messi’s defending champions Argentina to lift ⁠the trophy for a second time.

news.title: ‘Burnham bounce’ and World Cup lift mood in July, says data firm
news.lede: ‘Wave of optimism’ is sparked by prospect of new PM, England football team’s progress and hot weather. Consumer confidence in the UK jumped this month by its biggest margin for nearly three years as the prospect of Andy Burnham becoming prime minister became almost certain. The data company GfK said a “Burnham bounce” along with a strong run by the men’s England football team at the World Cup and sunny weather had lifted the mood of consumers in its long-running monthly survey. Burnham’s byelection victory on 18 June, which put the former mayor of Greater Manchester in pole position to take over from Keir Starmer, was credited with helping to improve consumers’ outlook for the economy over the next year by eight points.

news.title: Bouaddi, Moussa and the Arab World Cup stars set for moves in club football
news.lede: Following a historic eight-team Arab participation in the World Cup, several players from the Middle East and North Africa are hoping to make big moves during this summer’s transfer window. Morocco’s Ismail Saibari, who scored three goals in three games for the Atlas Lions at the World Cup, completed a switch from PSV Eindhoven to Bayern Munich last month, during the competition, while Egyptian star Mohamed Salah has everyone waiting on the announcement of his next destination following his Liverpool exit, with Besiktas emerging as the leading contender. news.title: The Remains of 39 Days
news.lede: As it ended, the 23rd edition of the FIFA World Cup revived an old argument: Can the sport ever be walled off from politics? Trouble shadowed the tournament from its early days—a US president intervening to have a player’s ban lifted, the FIFA chief admitting he had fretted over Argentina’s possible exit, and a banner unfurled after a semi-final reasserting Argentina’s claim over the Falklands (Las Malvinas). All of this added to suspicions that refereeing and stagecraft alike tilted towards expedience. Not for nothing Argentina, playing presumably Lionel Messi's last World Cup, drew the fiercest scrutiny: rival fans and commentators pointed to contentious VAR decisions in matches against Egypt and England as evidence of favouritism, even as the US investigates the Argentine Football Association’s (AFA) finances.
